final_codebook.domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification to lowest terms

skills.name: Align fraction units
skills.definition: Rewrite quantities into compatible fractional units for subtraction by finding a common denominator and/or expressing a whole number with a matching fractional part.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution finds an LCD/common denominator and converts one or more fractions to equivalent fractions.
Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0 over a stated denominator so whole and fractional parts can be subtracted together.
Tag when mixed-number fraction parts are rewritten to share a denominator before subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators already match and no unit-alignment rewriting is performed.
Do not tag for converting a nonstandard mixed number with an improper fractional part into a standard mixed number; that belongs to S02.
Do not tag for borrowing/regrouping after subtraction has begun.
Do not tag for reducing a result to lowest terms after subtraction.

skills.name: Normalize operands
skills.definition: Rewrite an operand into an equivalent standard form before subtraction, especially by converting a nonstandard mixed number with an improper fractional part into a standard mixed number.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a mixed number with an improper fraction part is rewritten as an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when the step explicitly cleans up an operand's form before the main subtraction rather than aligning denominators between operands.
Tag when operand rewriting changes the representation but not the value, in preparation for subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for finding a common denominator or converting fractions to equivalent fractions across operands; that belongs to S01.
Do not tag for rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a chosen denominator solely to match subtraction units; that belongs to S01.
Do not tag for borrowing/regrouping during subtraction.
Do not tag for final simplification of the answer.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Carry out the subtraction once quantities are in compatible form, including subtracting like-denominator fractions and subtracting whole and fractional parts of mixed numbers.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted over a common denominator.
Tag when whole parts and fraction parts are subtracted separately after setup is complete.
Tag when the subtraction step produces an intermediate negative fractional part that will later require regrouping.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for preparatory rewriting such as denominator alignment, whole-number rewriting, or mixed-number normalization.
Do not tag for borrowing/regrouping itself; that belongs to S04.
Do not tag for reducing a fraction or formatting the final answer in simplest form.

skills.name: Regroup and simplify
skills.definition: Resolve the subtraction result by borrowing/regrouping when needed and expressing the final answer in simplest valid form, including reduced fraction, mixed number, integer, or zero.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when 1 whole is borrowed from the whole part and converted into fractional units.
Tag when a negative or insufficient fractional part triggers regrouping before subtraction can be completed.
Tag when the post-subtraction result is simplified, reduced to lowest terms, converted from a zero fraction to 0, or written in final mixed-number/integer form.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for initial operand normalization before subtraction; that belongs to S02.
Do not tag for denominator alignment or rewriting to common units; that belongs to S01.
Do not tag for the raw subtraction step before regrouping or simplification; that belongs to S03.

decisions.reasoning: Both operations are setup actions that make fractional units compatible for subtraction. In this item set, rewriting a whole number as 0/n functions as the same alignment process as finding a common denominator, and keeping them separate would weaken independence and reduce Q-matrix parsimony.

decisions.details: Kept C02 as S02 with refined boundaries
decisions.reasoning: Normalization of nonstandard mixed numbers is a distinct pre-subtraction operation from denominator alignment. It is strongly supported by 3/3 consensus and appears in items that do not require common-denominator work, so it is independently testable.

The actual subtraction step is clearly distinct from setup and from regrouping/simplification. All experts agreed on this skill, and it provides essential explanatory coverage for the core arithmetic operation.

Borrowing/regrouping and final simplification were bundled by two experts and are needed to reach exactly four skills while preserving broad, diagnosable operations. Final simplification alone has weaker consensus and limited independent coverage, so combining it with post-subtraction resolution yields a clearer and more useful final-stage skill.

decisions.details: Removed C07 as a standalone skill
decisions.reasoning: Simplifying an operand fraction before subtraction appears in only one expert codebook and has weak evidence for independent diagnostic value. It is better absorbed under S02 as a special case of operand normalization rather than retained as a separate skill.

decisions.details: Refined S02 to focus on operand-standardization and clarified that whole-number rewriting for denominator matching belongs to S01
decisions.reasoning: Experts differed on whether whole-number rewriting belongs with alignment or normalization. The refined boundary improves annotator agreement: cross-operand unit matching is S01, while cleaning up a single operand's nonstandard form is S02.

summary: The final codebook consolidates the expert proposals into four broad, distinct skills that match the subtraction workflow: setup by aligning fraction units, setup by normalizing nonstandard operands, performing the subtraction, and resolving the result through regrouping and simplification. The main consolidation choices were to merge whole-number rewriting into denominator alignment, keep mixed-number normalization separate, and combine borrowing with final simplification to satisfy the four-skill constraint while maintaining clarity and diagnostic usefulness.
